title: What is Positron Emission Tomography (PET)?
description: The Positron Emission Tomographic technique (PET) is a nuclear medicine imaging test designed to examine human internal organs using radiopharmaceuticals (the most common of which is fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), which is injected into a patient

title: What are the opportunities and advantages of this technique?
description:
Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (PET-CT) is widely used in modern oncology and enables doctors 

  • Early diagnose existing neoplasms, respond quickly and prescribe treatment;
  • Assess the prevalence of cancer;
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of chemotherapy and radiation therapy for a given tumor and assist the treating physician in choosing further treatment strategies;
  • Helps to find the primary site of multiple metastatic lesions and to provide accurate diagnosis;
  • Distinguish between benign and malignant neoplasms;
  • Distinguish post-radiation residual fibrosis changes from active sites of malignancy.

title: When is it necessary to perform Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (PET/CT)?
description: It must be done on the doctor's instructions, at the initial stage of cancer diagnosis, during the treatment and after the completion of the treatment. Now, this technique is irreplaceable in oncology and is considered a golden standard.

title: How can I have a Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (PET/CT)?
description: To register, you need to visit the CJSC "Radioisotope Production Center" (address: 38/7 Halabyan Street, Yerevan) on working days from 9:00 to 18:00, or call +374 12 30 12 12. During the consultation, you should provide the doctor with the results of your previous imaging tests and medical history, if any. It is also necessary to strictly follow the doctor's instructions regarding the restriction of physical activity and diet. It is very important to be present at the examination at the appointed time.
